main_results.purpose: Exact blob-pinned transitive runtime graph preflight
Static exact-source proof of default-path process-epoch permit invalidation

result: The exact provenance runtime graph was pinned through its currently identified transitive role-local siblings, including the provenance wrapper, base runtime, compliance/provenance CLOSE layers, historical and provenance auditors, launch gates, attempt ledger, score wrapper, reserved-score pipeline, legacy reporting adapter, atomic frame codec, reporter, V3/K-guard core and StableSidecarJournalIO. Every listed Git blob was fetchable by exact SHA. Before full local byte execution, exact-source inspection found a blocking default-path liveness defect: durable_attempt_reservation_ledger_2026-08-28.py generates _BOOT_SECRET with secrets.token_bytes(32) at module import, but the provenance wrapper reloads a fresh base runtime for each public operation and the base runtime reloads a fresh attempt module for each reservation/launch operation. Thus reserve_and_issue normally MACs the permit under attempt-module secret A while launch_reserved_score validates it under independently generated secret B and fails before scorer execution. Dependency-injected campaigns that reuse one attempt module can mask this defect. The identified failure is fail-closed/liveness, not evidence inflation.
validated_contracts: The exact transitive graph currently needed by the default provenance runtime is connector-visible and blob-pinned; no identified filename/blob was missing from the role-local repository state.
The top-level provenance runtime does not cache _base(): each public operation executes a fresh base runtime module object unless base_runtime_module is injected.
The base runtime does not cache _default_attempt(): reserve_and_issue and launch_reserved_score each execute a fresh durable_attempt_reservation_ledger module unless attempt_module is injected.

The attempt module generates a fresh 32-byte _BOOT_SECRET at import, signs permits with it in acknowledge_reservation and checks the current module secret in validate_launch_permit before ledger validation.

Therefore preserving the same attempt module/process-epoch secret across RESERVE -> SCORE is a necessary default-runtime liveness condition. A process restart may still intentionally invalidate in-memory permits under the fail-closed policy.
measurement_validity_rules: Exact-runtime integration must test the default wrapper path, not only dependency-injected paths; injection can accidentally stabilize process-local state and hide reload defects.
Process-epoch authorization state must be stable within one process lifecycle but must not silently become durable across restart when recovery policy requires fail-closed no-relaunch.

A dynamic import helper that always module_from_spec/exec_module's a module containing random process-local state is semantically different from importing that module once, even when the source blob is identical.
Treat the current defect as liveness/fail-closed until evidence shows a path that admits a score under mismatched authorization; do not overstate it as a false-positive statistical failure.
Do not substitute a simplified semantic runtime for the blocked exact default path. Preserve blob-pinned bytes and record execution/tooling gaps explicitly.
scope_limitations: The module-reload defect is established by exact blob-pinned source control flow, not by executing the complete repository-local sibling graph in one Python directory during this invocation.
The connected repository exposes source content through the connector but not as a local filesystem mount/export to the container runtime, so full byte import/execution remained unavailable here.
A caller that explicitly reuses the same base_runtime_module/attempt_module object can avoid the observed secret mismatch; this does not validate the documented default wrapper path.
No claim is made about distributed storage behavior beyond the prior checkpoint; this run focused on exact runtime module identity/process-epoch semantics.
frontier: Create a process-stable blob-pinned runtime context/registry that imports each exact sibling once per process and injects the same attempt module through ADMIT/RESERVE/SCORE/SLOT/COMMIT/CLOSE while preserving restart invalidation.

Byte-execute RESERVE -> SCORE on the exact default wrapper before and after the stable-context change; require the current default to reproduce permit-MAC rejection and the fixed path to execute the scorer exactly once.

After fixing within-process module identity, resume the two-slot StableSidecarJournalIO campaign and inject crashes around SLOT fsync, COMMIT fsync and CLOSE fsync with exact compliance replay after restart.
Verify that any module-cache/context fix is blob-identity checked and cannot accidentally reuse stale code after a configured process restart or semantic control change.
exact_next_action: Implement a role-local candidate runtime context that verifies the exact Git blob SHA of each sibling before one-time import, stores one attempt-module instance for the process epoch, and routes the provenance runtime operations with explicit module injection. First test the minimal same-process RESERVE -> SCORE path: one durable reservation must yield one valid permit and exactly one scorer call. Then simulate process restart by constructing a new context and require the old permit to fail while durable reservation recovery remains fail-closed. Only after those two checks resume the full two-slot stable-sidecar lifecycle.
